svg.title: Agent multi-step tool loop — PLAN, concurrent EXECUTE, SYNTHESIZE; step guard and step failure

g.text: Agent multi-step tool loop — PLAN, concurrent EXECUTE, SYNTHESIZE; step guard and step failure
1 · PLAN — one shot, one retry, then a degraded fallback
(agent.py:213-214) and logs nothing. A deep multi-tool request silently
collapses into one plain completion, and the user is never told: the
degraded plan streams a normal answer with route "agent".
MAX-ITERATION GUARD — there is no iteration.
no step can enqueue another, so the loop cannot run away. The bound is
· the prompt budget step_budget(effort): medium 5, high 8 (agent.py:42, :48)
if either prompt constant is reworded, the budget silently stops applying.
_STEP_BUDGET and _SYNTH_TOKENS have no "fast"/"low" keys, so an explicit
agent=true at effort "fast" silently gets the medium values.
2 · EXECUTE — asyncio.gather over the plan, at most 3 at a time
F7 — the `web` gate is enforced only at plan time.
not forward `web` (agent.py:571-580), so a step that survived coercion
still reaches the live web branch at agent.py:337.
[for each PlanStep, up to STEP_CONCURRENCY = 3 concurrently (agent.py:378-381)]
— the synthesizer is handed `f"SQL result ({len(rows)} row(s)):"`
no statement that this is a sample
(agent.py:258-274). The direct SQL route carries an explicit "you are
shown only the FIRST FEW ROWS, quote the true row count" instruction
(sql.py:267-278), added because "314 rows came back and the summary said
29 records". The agent path never got that fix.
Closed gate: when mode == "assistant" the planner is given
Degradation is invisible: SalesforceUnavailable / UnsafeSoql return a
prose apology and an empty sub-meta, yet the step still reports
— agent.py:312-335 is a byte-equivalent duplicate of this branch
behind the identical condition: 24 lines of unreachable dead code.
through** (agent.py:351-352) into the llm tail: the step answers from
model knowledge, is reported status="done", and carries
search_unavailable flag — unlike the direct search route, which sets
Fetched page content is untrusted and reaches the model prompt.
[kind == "llm", or the web branch fell through]
F5 — raw exception text is streamed to the browser
(agent.py:388-392): stack-free but unsanitised, and it may carry SOQL,
SQL, hostnames or driver messages. Nothing is logged server-side.
This is one of eleven bare `except` sites in the core-4 engines,
— because return_exceptions is not set, a BaseException that escapes
aborts the gather and leaves the sibling coroutines
their Salesforce queries and page fetches complete with nobody listening.
Concurrent steps also share one `emit` callable, so research events from
parallel web steps interleave into a single frontend panel with no step id
3 · SYNTHESIZE — one merged answer, one merged meta
Sources without a `url` are skipped (agent.py:435-437), leaving their local
[n] markers unmapped and pointing at whichever page ends up with that
step with a truthy `sql` contributes the
on record_id, report files on filename, sources on url (agent.py:494-510).
Nothing enforces "exactly one meta per turn" at runtime — there is no engine
ABC, no Protocol and no return-type check anywhere; the contract is pure duck
No timeout exists anywhere in agent.py.
engines/*.py hits only url.py:36 and search.py:315/338. The single bound is
the 300 s httpx client timeout (llm.py:78, config.py:264).
Worst case for ONE user message: plan 2 x 300 s, then ceil(8/3) = 3 waves of
(per-step model call + Salesforce/web fetch), then the synthesis stream —
, with the only cancellation path being the user
Model-call budget at 8 steps: 1-2 plan + 1 per llm/rag/web step + 1-2 per sql
Red-bordered box = trust boundary (traffic leaving the host).
Solid arrow = call · dashed arrow = return value.
Red note = swallowed exception, silent degradation or missing timeout.
Amber note = design constraint or bound worth auditing.
Fn labels are the finding ids from docs/_evidence/orch-engines-core4.md.
